notes.meaning: Worship begins with a call to give thanks to the LORD because goodness is His very nature. Everything He does comes from this goodness, especially His steady love toward His people. That mercy never runs out, but lasts from generation to generation.

The Lord is praised above all rulers, angels, and false gods. He holds supreme power over every earthly king and heavenly power. Because His mercy lasts forever, His great rule is full of care and justice rather than harshness.

God alone works great miracles, without needing help or advice from anyone else. Every wonder He performs shows His almighty power. These works also serve His loving purpose to help and save His people.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that God acted alone when creating the world, whereas His later miracles in history were performed through human servants and angels.

notes.meaning: God used deep wisdom to shape the skies, giving the earth the air and weather it needs to support life. He also lifted the dry land up out of the deep waters so people would have a safe, solid home. Both heavens and earth stand as proof of His ongoing kindness to mankind.

God created the sun, moon, and stars to give light to the world in an orderly way. The sun warms and brightens the day, while the moon and stars guide travellers and bring comfort through the dark night. These dependable lights shine as daily reminders of His faithful love.

God's final plague struck down the firstborn sons of Egypt, finally breaking Pharaoh's stubborn refusal to free the Hebrews. This heavy judgment on an oppressive nation was actually an act of mercy toward Israel. It showed that God will not let His oppressed people remain in chains forever.

The Lord brought the entire nation of Israel out from the middle of Egypt, leaving not a single person behind in slavery. He did this with an outstretched arm, which pictures a workman putting out His full strength in public view. His power was put to work so that His loving promise would never fail.

God split the Red Sea into two parts to make an open path between the walls of water. He gave the Israelites courage to walk through the deep seabed and brought them safely to the other side. When Pharaoh's army chased them, God shook the pursuers off into the waves, saving His people from destruction.

The Lord guided His people across a harsh, waterless desert for forty years. He supplied food from heaven, brought water from rocks, and kept them on the right path. His mercy never gave up on them, even when they doubted and complained.

Israel had to face strong, famous rulers who tried to block their way into the promised land. The Lord struck these kings down because no human army can stand against His plans. Their defeat showed that God values the rescue of His people far more than the pride of worldly kings.

Sihon and Og were two well-known kings east of the Jordan River who attacked the Israelites. Though Og was a giant and Sihon commanded a strong army, both were quickly overcome by the Lord. God gave His people victory over one enemy after another so they would trust Him completely.

The Lord took the lands of these defeated kings and gave them to Israel as an inheritance. The tribes received this good home as a gift from their Master, not by their own power alone. This gift of land served as an early picture of the eternal rest and heavenly home God prepares for His own.

God kept His people in mind when they were crushed, weak, and held in captivity. He stepped in with power and snatched them out of the grip of their enemies. In the same way, God remembers sinners in their lost condition and frees them from sin and death through Christ.

The Lord's kindness extends beyond His chosen nation to every living creature on the earth. He faithfully provides daily food for beasts, birds, and humans alike. If God cares so tenderly for common animals, His people can be sure He will never fail to care for them.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine linked the food given to all creatures to spiritual nourishment, pointing to Christ as the true Bread of Life who offers salvation to all nations.

notes.meaning: The psalm closes by urging everyone to praise the God of heaven, who sits exalted above all earthly trouble. Every good gift comes down from His throne of glory. His loving devotion is a spring that never runs dry, and believers will sing of it forever.
